```{r, warning=FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
library(kableExtra)
library(car)
library(readr)
library(GGally)
library(ggpubr)
library(caret)
library(knitr)
library(tidyr)
library(MASS)

set.seed(1)
cars <- read_csv("car details v4.csv")

#split engine cc number and change into numeric instead of string
cars$Engine <- sub(" .*", "", cars$Engine)
cars$Engine = as.numeric(cars$Engine)

#split horsepower and convert to numeric
cars$`Max Power` <- sub(" .*", "", cars$`Max Power`)
cars$`Max Power` = as.numeric(cars$`Max Power`)

#split max torque and convert to numeric
cars$`Max Torque` <- sub(" .*", "", cars$`Max Torque`)
cars$`Max Torque` = as.numeric(cars$`Max Torque`)

#convert first, second, and third into numeric
cars$Owner <- ifelse(cars$Owner == "First", 1, 
                   ifelse(cars$Owner == "Second", 2, 
                          ifelse(cars$Owner == "Third", 3, cars$Owner)))
cars$Owner = as.numeric(cars$Owner)

conversion_rate <- 83
# Convert the price from Rupees to USD
cars$Price <- cars$Price / conversion_rate

#remove N/A and Unregistered Car
cars <- na.omit(cars)
cars <- subset(cars, Owner != "UnRegistered Car")
```

```{r}
#summary of variables and pair plots
df = data.frame(cars$Price, cars$Year, cars$Kilometer, cars$Owner,
                cars$Engine, cars$`Max Power`, cars$`Max Torque`, cars$Length,
                cars$Height, cars$Width, cars$`Fuel Tank Capacity`)

ggpairs(df)
ggpairs(df,
        title = "Scatter Plot Matrix of Variables",
        upper = list(continuous = "points"),
        lower = list(continuous = "smooth"),
        diag = list(continuous = "barDiag"))

summary_stats <- df %>%
  summarise_all(list(
    Mean = ~mean(.),
    Median = ~median(.),
    SD = ~sd(.),
    Min = ~min(.),
    Max = ~max(.),
    `1st Qu.` = ~quantile(., 0.25),
    `3rd Qu.` = ~quantile(., 0.75)
  )) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(),
               names_to = c("Variable", "Statistic"),
               names_sep = "_") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Statistic, values_from = value)

# Format the table
kable(summary_stats, caption = "Summary Statistics for Multiple Variables") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))

```


```{r}
#remove outliers
cars <- cars %>%
  filter(Kilometer <= 400000)

cars <- cars %>%
  filter(Year >= 2000)

cars <- cars %>%
  filter(Price <= 100000)
```


```{r}
#fitting first model with all numerical variables
first_model = lm(Price~Year + Kilometer + `Seating Capacity` +
                   `Fuel Tank Capacity` + Engine + Owner + `Max Torque` +
                   `Max Power` + Length + Width + Height, data = cars)

summary_1 = summary(first_model)

summary_1

#using stepwise to determine number and order of predictors
stepwise_model <- step(first_model, direction = "both")
```


```{r}
#fitting second model based on stepwise
second_model = lm(Price ~ Year + Kilometer + `Seating Capacity` +
                    `Fuel Tank Capacity` + Engine + `Max Torque` +
                    `Max Power` + Height, data = cars)

summary(second_model)

#vif for multicollinearity
table = vif(second_model)
vif_df <- data.frame(VIF = table)

kable(vif_df, caption = "Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) Results")%>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = F)
```

#### VIF for Engine, Power, and Torque are high, sugests collinearity, create new models with only one of each to compare which is best

```{r}
#third model accounting for multicollinearity, k-fold for validation
set.seed(123)
mod1 = lm(Price ~ Year + Kilometer + `Seating Capacity` + `Fuel Tank Capacity`
          + Engine + Height, data = cars)

mod2 = lm(Price ~ Year + Kilometer + `Seating Capacity` + `Fuel Tank Capacity`
          + `Max Power` + Height, data = cars)

mod3 = lm(Price ~ Year + Kilometer + `Seating Capacity` + `Fuel Tank Capacity`
          + `Max Torque` + Height, data = cars)


train_control <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10)  # 10-fold cross-validation

# Train the model using cross-validation
model1 <- train(Price ~ Year + Kilometer + `Seating Capacity` +
                  `Fuel Tank Capacity` + Engine + Height, data = cars,
                method = "rf", trControl = train_control)

model2 <- train(Price ~ Year + Kilometer + `Seating Capacity` +
                  `Fuel Tank Capacity` + `Max Power` + Height, data = cars,
                method = "rf", trControl = train_control)

model3 <- train(Price ~ Year + Kilometer + `Seating Capacity` +
                  `Fuel Tank Capacity` + `Max Torque` + Height, data = cars,
                method = "rf", trControl = train_control)

# Print the results
print(model1)
print(model2)
print(model3)
```

```{r}
#fitting third model and checking for assumptions
third_model = lm(Price ~ Year + Kilometer + `Seating Capacity` +
                   `Fuel Tank Capacity` + `Max Power` + Height, data = cars)

summary(third_model)

residuals <- resid(third_model)

#Q-Q plot for normality
ggplot(data.frame(residuals = residuals), aes(sample = residuals)) +
  geom_qq() +
  geom_qq_line() +
  ggtitle("Q-Q Plot of Residuals") +
  theme_minimal()

#resid plot for constant variance
fitted_values <- fitted(third_model)
ggplot(data.frame(fitted_values = fitted_values, residuals = residuals),
       aes(x = fitted_values, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs. Fitted Values",
       x = "Fitted Values",
       y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#boxcox transformation
bc_transform = boxcox(third_model)

 bc_val = bc_transform$x[which.max(bc_transform$y)]
bc_val

transformed_price = log(cars$Price,10)


fourth_model = lm(transformed_price ~ Year + Kilometer + `Seating Capacity`
                  + `Fuel Tank Capacity` + `Max Power` + Height, data = cars)

residuals <- resid(fourth_model)
fitted_values <- fitted(fourth_model)

#new qq plot
ggplot(data.frame(residuals = residuals), aes(sample = residuals)) +
  geom_qq() +
  geom_qq_line() +
  ggtitle("Q-Q Plot of Residuals (Transformed)") +
  theme_minimal()

#new resid plot
ggplot(data.frame(fitted_values = fitted_values, residuals = residuals),
       aes(x = fitted_values, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs. Fitted Values (Transformed)",
       x = "Fitted Values",
       y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal()

summary(fourth_model)
```
